Sample fine tea, attend presentations by tea authors and industry experts, and shop for tea supplies at the Northwest Tea Festival in Seattle Center Exhibition Hall, 301 Mercer St. in Seattle. Children age 12 and younger are free.

map photos video

Tour art studios  FREE

September 26 - 27, 2026 (10 a.m. to 6 p.m.)

Snohomish (30 miles NE)

Drive to 16 studios displaying the work of 27 artists during Snohomish Studio Tour. Some locations have coffee, snacks, art projects, and live music.

studio map

Beer & BBQ festival

September 26 - 27, 2026 (11 a.m. to 5 p.m.)

Enumclaw (43 miles SE)

Your ticket to BBQ, Brews, & Brats includes 3 samples of BBQ (choice of pork, brisket, chicken, ribs), with or without 3 samples of beer. Expect live music, vendors, and a free kids’ zone at Enumclaw Expo Center, 45224 284th Ave. SE in Enumclaw.

map tickets

Bellingham festival  FREE

September 26 - 27, 2026

Bellingham (90 miles N)

Bellingham SeaFeast features local seafood such as salmon, a beverage garden (beer, wine, cider), live music, art vendors, a free 5K run, a pinball tournament, boat rides (not free), and speakers at Zuanich Point Park, 2600 N Harbor Loop Drive in Bellingham.

map photos video

Halloween at Wild Waves

September 26 - Nov. 1, 2026

Federal Way (27 miles S)

Wild Waves has two options on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays at 36201 Enchanted Pkwy S in Federal Way. Children younger than age 18 must be with an adult age 21+.

  • Starts Sept. 26 — Booville offers daytime trick-or-treating, face-painting and entertainment for age 12 and younger, Sat. & Sun.
  • Starts Oct. 2 — Fright Fest offers scary monsters, rides in the dark, and haunted houses at night, Fri., Sat., Sun. Adult beverages.

map photos video

Wine fun run

September 27, 2026

Woodinville (18 miles NE)

Run or Wine is a 5K/10K urban run/walk that includes wine tasting (or beer/cider), a race photo to download, and post-race snacks beginning at Dragonfly Sculpture Bridge, 14735 NE 145th St. in Woodinville. Repeats several times a year.

map photos

Bonsai party

September 27, 2026 (1 to 4 p.m.)

Federal Way (25 miles S)

A $175 ticket to Branch Out includes appetizers, drinks, dessert, live jazz, Taiko drumming, Chinese dance, a live auction, and a curated selection of bonsai trees in the iconic former Weyerhaeuser Headquarters at 33663 Weyerhaeuser Way S in Federal Way.

map tickets photos

Senior citizen festival  FREE

September 29, 2026

Sand Point (7.6 miles NE)

Visit the booths of 100 organizations that serve seniors, and attend workshops during Seattle Senior Resource Fair in Hangar 30 at Magnuson Park, 6310 NE 74th St. in Seattle. Free parking.

map

Charity tasting

September 30, 2026 (5:30 to 9 p.m.)

Central District (1.5 miles SE)

A $250 ticket to Omnivorous includes “unlimited food and drink tastings from 20 local culinary standouts,” with DJ music and storytelling to support affordable housing at Washington Hall, 153 14th Ave. in Seattle for age 21+. Dress semi-formal or in cocktail attire.

The Modern Mediterranean Table

Duration: 3 hoursType: In-PersonPrice: $145

Fresh and vibrant, Mediterranean ingredients easily intermingle with techniques from around the globe. Join Stefan Milne and learn how dishes can incorporate kelp or miso and still taste distinctly Mediterranean as you make Albacore tuna ceviche with olives, charred scallion oil, basil, and gem lettuce; marinated cucumber and summer melon with pistachio miso cream and dukkah; clams with homemade ‘nduja, kelp-tomato broth and grilled sourdough; and almond cake with burnt honey, orange blossom and stone fruit.


Please note: some classes can be adjusted for students with dietary restrictions, but many cannot. If you’re vegetarian, pescatarian, or gluten-free, you can use the drop-down menu on our events page to view the best classes to fit your needs. If a class you’re interested in doesn’t appear in that filtered view, please email us before registering and we’ll see if the class’s menu can be modified.

Whole Grain Breads

Duration: 3½ hoursType: In-PersonPrice: $145

It’s difficult to improve upon homemade bread, but Vindi Rathnayake is here to open up a whole new world of baking with whole grains. In this class you'll learn the fundamentals of working with whole grain flours, mixing and kneading dough, and common problems when baking with whole grains — including how to overcome them! She’ll cover shaping techniques and proper proofing as you make loaves of seeded whole grain artisan bread; honey and oat porridge sandwich bread; and soft honey and olive wholemeal dinner buns that students will turn into tomato, arugula, ham, and halloumi sandwiches with dill pickle aioli.

Family Dinner: A Pacific Northwest Mushroom Feast

Price: $165

Join us for a dinner where we do all the cooking! Each month we open the doors between our classrooms and seat 40 guests for a five-course family-style dinner, featuring all the ingredients we’re excited about. This season we’re celebrating our favorite Pacific Northwest ingredient: mushrooms! Pricing includes a wine or nonalcoholic drink pairing with each savory course, and tea or coffee with dessert.


Chanterelle and crab croquettes with savory fish sauce citrus curd
Caramelized fennel and sherry-glazed maitake mushroom toasts with lemon-thyme ricotta

Lobster mushroom galette
Caramelized onion, creme fraiche, and mizuna

Kombu-brined Cornish game hen
Shimeiji duxelle, salt roasted leeks, chanterelles, and turnips

Matsutake and French green lentils
Pickled oyster mushrooms, endive, walnuts, and sherry vinaigrette

Steamed sweet dumplings with maple and star anise-roasted plums
Candy cap mushroom creme anglaise


The vegetarian menu will include mushroom-glazed crispy tofu in place of the game hen.

The pescatarian menu will include kombu-wrapped black cod in place of the game hen.

The gluten-free menu will include gluten-free bread in the mushroom toast, gluten-free dough in the galette, and gluten-free dumplings in the dessert.

The Jordanian Table: Mansaf

Duration: 3 hoursType: In-PersonPrice: $145

Join Nadia Tommalieh for a journey into the heart of Jordanian hospitality through its most iconic dish. In this class, you’ll explore the cultural roots and rituals surrounding mansaf as you learn to prepare it, from slowly braising lamb shanks in a rich, tangy sauce made from jameed (dried yogurt) to serving the lamb over turmeric- and ghee-scented rice, nestled on top of shrak, a delicate Bedouin flatbread. To complete your Jordanian table you’ll prepare galayet bandoura (sautéed ripe tomatoes with garlic, olive oil, and chili, served with crispy pita chips); zaiytoon (green olives marinated in lemon, jalapeño, turmeric, and olive oil); mkhalel left (bright pink pickled turnips in brine); and, for dessert, awameh (light, crispy dough balls soaked in orange blossom syrup and sprinkled with crushed pistachios).

Please note: some classes can be adjusted for students with dietary restrictions, but many cannot. If you’re vegetarian, pescatarian, or gluten-free, you can use the drop-down menu on our events page to view the best classes to fit your needs. The Mexican Bakery: Pan de Muerto

Duration: 3 hoursType: In-PersonPrice: $140

Rich in indigenous history, Dia de los muertos is a two-day holiday in Mexico where family and friends welcome back the souls of loved ones that have passed. There is a lot of color, ceremony, and of course, plenty of delicious food to enjoy. In the days leading up to this holiday, Gino Garcia – author of Disney Pixar’s Coco: The Official Cookbook – will teach you about the traditional spiced sweet breads prepared for this holiday. You’ll make fluffy pan de yema (“egg yolk bread,” flavored with orange, anise seed, cinnamon, and vanilla) that you’ll shape into pan de muerto negro (the popular “skull and bones” shape) decorated with corn husk ashes and marigold flowers; pan de yema de alfeñique (Oaxacan-style bread decorated with sesame seeds and candy skull); and pan de animas (Guanajuato-style “soul bread” shaped like a person, glazed with meringue and strawberry sugar). You’ll enjoy your freshly baked treats with cajeta de muerto (guava and sweet potato butter) and chocolate de agua (cinnamon-spiced drinking chocolate).

Mandu: Korean Dumplings

Duration: 3 hoursType: In-PersonPrice: $145

There’s a dumpling in every culture, and in Korea - that’s mandu! Making mandu is a legendary family affair in Korea, with multiple generations rolling, filling, and shaping dumplings during holidays and family gatherings. These delicious parcels symbolize good fortune and longevity and you can join Jee Hye Kang in this shared communal activity and learn how to make from-scratch! You'll make 만두피 (mandu wrappers) that you’ll turn into 김치만두 kimchi mandu; 새우 부추 만두 (shrimp and chive mandu); and 왕만두 wang mandu (“King Dumplings” filled with mushrooms and vegetables). You’ll enjoy them with 만두국 mandu guk (mandu soup); 초간장 cho ganjang (soy sauce and vinegar dipping sauce); and roasted Korean sweet potatoes for dessert.

Persian Winter Solstice

Rooted in ancient tradition, Shab-e Yalda honors the return of light and the hope that carries us through darkness. Join Omid Roustaei in celebrating Shab-e Yalda, the Persian winter solstice and the longest night of the year. We’ll explore the rituals, stories, and symbolism of this beloved celebration, including its vibrant table of pomegranates, watermelon, persimmons, nuts, and dried fruits.
